exactQuote: Aigul Utepova is a well-known Kazakh freelance investigative journalist who has worked for the independent online outlets NewTimes.KZ and Saryagash Info in addition to publishing content on her Facebook account and YouTube channel, Aigul TV, each of which has 8,000 followers. 115 Utepova’s reporting has addressed social and political issues, including the government’s response to COVID-19.
explanation: 报告称 Aigul Utepova 为哈萨克斯坦自由调查记者，报道社会及政治议题；并非由系统把博主身份推定为记者。

exactQuote: On September 15, 2020, a criminal investigation against Utepova was opened under Article 405(2) of the Criminal Code on the basis of her supposed participation in the activities of the banned DCK and Koshe opposition parties.
explanation: 报告记载 2020-09-15 因当局指称其参与被禁组织而启动刑事调查；指控内容不等于系统认定事实成立。

exactQuote: Following this decision, the authorities continued to request extensions of house arrest as the pretrial investigation continued , all of which were approved by the investiga tive court, meaning that Utepova remained under house arrest until her trial started and throughout the trial – a total of seven and a half months.
explanation: 报告记载居家限制多次延长，持续至审判期间；后来离开精神医疗机构并未解除全部限制。

exactQuote: In response to a complaint against t he November 11 decision filed by defense counsel, as well as a prosecution petition stating that the investigative court erred in imposing preventive security measures on Utepova,149 a judge amended the ruling to “exclude the application of the safety measure,” finding that it exceeded the investigator’s request.
explanation: 辩护律师投诉与检方纠错申请均被报告记载。法官排除安全措施是部分程序变化，不能把辩护投诉单独当作所有后续结果的原因。

exactQuote: The judge, however, authorized Utepova’s continued observation and examination, with the result that she was forced to remain at the facility. 151 Utepova was released on December 11, 2020.
explanation: 调整裁定后仍必须留院观察检查，直到 2020-12-11 离开该机构。出院不是撤案、无罪或解除居家限制。

exactQuote: At the March 15 hearing, U tepova pled not guilty and asked the judge to allow her to take 5 –10 minute daily walks while the trial was ongoing, as she remained under house arrest.157 The judge replied that the court “cannot change the preventative measure until the final decision on the case.”
explanation: 2021-03-15 当事人请求每天短暂散步，法官答复当时不能更改措施；这只是特定请求的回应。

exactQuote: On March 25, 2021, the defense raised concerns regardi ng procedural irregularities, including the alleged retrieval of information from Utepova’s phone and computer without a court order. 161 In this regard, the defense moved to question one of the lead investigators, O spanov (first name unknown) .162 The defense also reiterated the prosecutor’s obligation to clarify the date of the Koshe ban.
explanation: 2021-03-25 辩护方提出程序异议并申请询问调查员，材料并不显示这一申请令案件终结。

exactQuote: Defense counsel responded that the expert opinions were unreliable because the experts did not “know their subject matter.”193 The defense further stated that Utepova was being prosecuted for her journalistic work and for expressing her opinions, in violation of her rights.
explanation: 辩护方质疑专家可靠性，并主张起诉涉及其新闻工作及意见表达。

exactQuote: On April 29, 2021, the court delivered its verdict, pronouncing Utepova guilty and sentencing her to “restriction of freedom for a period of 1 year, with the establishment of probation supervision, depriving her of the right to engage in social and political activities, including with the use of mass media and telecommunication networks, for a period of 2 years.”195 Utepova was also sentenced to 100 hours of “forced labor.”
explanation: 一审定罪，判处一年限制自由、两年社会政治活动和媒体相关活动限制，另有100小时强制劳动；这是报告中的历史判决。

exactQuote: In June 2021, an appeals court rejected Utepova’s appeal against her conviction.
explanation: 2021年6月上诉被驳回；报告未提供精确日期。未由此推断后来所有救济途径的最终结果。

exactQuote: The Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch Initiative deployed a monitor to observe the trial of Aigul Utepova before the Saryarka District Court of Nur -Sultan. The trial was held over Zoom. The monitor was fluent in Russian and Kazakh and able to understand the proceedings. The monitor did not experience an y impediments in logging onto the video feed and was present for the entirety of the trial, which started on March 15, 2021 and concluded with Utepova’s conviction on April 29, 2021 (hearings on March 15, 25, & 29 and April 5, 7, 13, 14, 24, 28, & 29).
explanation: TrialWatch 派员远程观察 2021年3—4月审判；监测和后续报告本身不证明改变了司法结果。

exactQuote: Kazakh laws on commitment to psychiatric institutions – whether civil or criminal – must be amended to provide comprehensive due process protections.
explanation: 报告作者提出修改精神医疗收治法律的建议，不是已经完成的法律改革。

exactQuote: Ms. Chargui is a Tunisian blogger and self -described liberal woma n who does not subscribe to any religious beliefs.
explanation: Emna Chargui 在报告中被称为博主；未据此归类为记者。

exactQuote: On May 3, 2020, Ms. Chargui posted a photo of a poem entitled “ Verse of Corona” (“Surat Al-Corona”) to her personal Facebook page, after seeing it posted on other social media accounts. As Ms. Chargui has explained, she shared the poem with her friends on Facebook for “fun and entertainment” but deleted it the same day after receiving comments from other Facebook users insulting her and threatening to violently assault and kill her.38 Ms. Chargui also received rape threats.
explanation: 2020-05-03 转发疫情讽刺诗后收到威胁，随后删除帖子；这是案情背景，非倡导行动成效。

exactQuote: On May 5, 2020, Ms. Ines Trabelsi was accredited as Ms. Chargui’s defense attorney and accompanied the defendant to a hearing before the judicial police.
explanation: 律师 Ines Trabelsi 于 2020-05-05 陪同司法警察讯问，不能扩大为其在所有审前讯问中均有律师在场。

exactQuote: On May 6, 2020, Ms. Chargui was interrogated in court by at least seven members of the Public Prosecutor’s Office: her lawyer was not allowed to accompany her
explanation: 报告区分翌日检方讯问：律师未获准陪同。一次获得律师协助不代表该问题已全面解决。

exactQuote: The trial, originally set for May 28, 2020 before the Tunis Court of First Instance , was adjourned due to the COVID-19 pandemic, resuming on July 2, 2020. The proceedings were public and lasted one day. In response to questioning by the presiding judge, Ms. Chargui testified that she was not the author of the “Verse of Corona” but found it on Facebook and shared it on her personal page because she thought it was funny. 51 She emphasized that she meant it as a joke and did not intend to attack or harm the beliefs of others.52 Ms. Chargui was represented at trial by a defense team consisting of approximately ten lawyers, who argued that an acquittal was warranted because, among
explanation: 原定审判因疫情延期，2020-07-02 恢复；约十名律师参与庭审辩护并主张无罪。该段需结合下一页了解理由。

exactQuote: other things, the case violated the defendant’s constitutional rights to freedom of expression and privacy, the impugned conduct did not meet the requirements of Articles 52 and 53 of Decree 115 of 2011, and the prosecution violated the principle of legality.
explanation: 庭审辩护主张涉及表达与隐私权、构成要件以及罪刑法定；这是辩护意见，不是法院采纳结果。

exactQuote: On July 13, 2020 the Court issued its verdict convicting Ms. Chargui of both offenses and sentencing her to six months in prison and a fine of 2,000 dinars.
explanation: 本页将宣判记为2020-07-13，判处六个月监禁和罚金；与方法页日期冲突，系统不任选一天。

exactQuote: Ms. Chargui subsequently sought and obtained asylum in Germany.
explanation: 报告记载后来获得德国庇护，未记具体日期。庇护与撤销突尼斯定罪是不同结果。

exactQuote: While Ms. Chargui’s lawyers registered an appeal within 10 days of the first-instance judgment, as provided by law, they will not be permitted to defend her before the appeals court if she is not in attendance and the court may in its discretion decide to proceed in absentia (without either Ms. Chargui or her lawyers). The appeal is still pending.
explanation: 律师在一审判决后提起上诉；截至报告时未决。报告中的10天只作为历史原文保留，不能成为新案期限计算规则。

exactQuote: The monitor did not experience any impediments in entering the courtroom and was present for the entirety of the trial, which consisted of a hearing on July 2, 2020 and the delivery of the verdict on July 3, 2020.
explanation: 方法部分将判决宣读记为2020-07-03，与PDF14页2020-07-13不一致。

exactQuote: The Clooney Foundation for Justice deployed a monitor to the trial of Emna Chargui before the Tunis Court of First Instance. The monitor spoke Arabic and was able to follow the proceedings.
explanation: TrialWatch 派出懂阿拉伯语的观察员观察庭审。这是实际监测行动，未记载对判决产生的独立效果。

exactQuote: To assist in a reform process, Tunisia should invite the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Expression and /or the UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Religion or Belief for a country visit and fully implement their recommendations.
explanation: 报告建议突尼斯邀请联合国特别报告员进行国别访问；不是特别报告员已介入本案，也不等同个人申诉已获受理。

exactQuote: Myriam Bribri is a 34-year-old fashion designer,26 blogger, and anti-impunity activist.
explanation: 报告明确身份为服装设计师、博主和反有罪不罚活动人士，没有把她称为记者。

exactQuote: Ms. Bribri is facing charges under Article 86 of the Telecommunications Code for “offend[ing] security officials.” The charges stem from expletive -laced comments that she posted on social media in response to a video circulating of a police officer beating someone. The next hearing in her case is on June 28.
explanation: 报告时因回应警察暴力视频的社交媒体言论面临电信法第86条指控，听证尚待举行。

exactQuote: On October 7, Ms. Bribri received an official summons for investigation from the Judicial Police in Sfax. 35 She was questioned by the Judicial Police the next morning.
explanation: 2020-10-07收到正式传唤，次日接受司法警察讯问。

exactQuote: After arriving at the courthouse, Ms. Bribri waited over two hours before her lawyers were informed that Ms. Bribri’s trial would proceed that very day. 39 Defense counsel requested to postpone the heari ng, which was rescheduled to December 14, 2020.
explanation: 律师得知当天即开庭后申请延期，听证改期至2020-12-14；这只是程序性结果，不能记作撤诉。

exactQuote: Subsequently, the hearing on December 14 was delayed until February 8 due to judicial strikes and then again to April 12 due to a COVID -19 ordinance requiring courts to only hear cases in which accused are d etained. On April 12, defense counsel requested an adjournment for further preparation. The hearing was postponed to June 28.
explanation: 2021-04-12 律师申请更多准备时间，听证延期至6月28日；终局结果未记载。

exactQuote: One such prosecution is that of Myriam Bribri, which the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative has been monitoring.
explanation: 报告明确 TrialWatch 正在监测该案；监测起始日期及独立效果未记载。

exactQuote: The court should dismiss the case against Myriam Bribri, or the prosecution should withdraw the charges.
explanation: 作者呼吁法院驳回或检方撤回指控，是报告建议，不能标成已撤诉。

exactQuote: Tunisia should invite the UN Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of freedom of opinion and expression to make a country visit, following which the Rapporteur can provide recommendations for how to bring the Tunisian legal framework in line with international and regional obligations.
explanation: 作者建议邀请联合国表达自由特别报告员国别访问，未记载邀请或访问已实施。

exactQuote: In August 2018, Shahidul Alam, a prominent photojournalist and social activist in Bangladesh, was arrested for commenting on and showing pictures he had taken of student protests in a Facebook Live video post and for discussing socio-political tensions that sparked the protests in a television interview.
explanation: 报告将 Alam 记为摄影记者和社会活动人士，并将逮捕背景与其抗议报道、Facebook 直播和电视评论相连；不将警方指控视为已经证实。

exactQuote: The High Court ultimately ordered Alam’s release on bail on November 15, 2018.
explanation: 报告明确的是 2018-11-15 高等法院准予保释的裁定；不把裁定日擅自当成实际离开监所的日期。

exactQuote: As referenced above, Ahmed filed a complaint on August 7, 2018 with the NHRC regarding Alam’s allegations of torture.
explanation: Alam 的妻子 Rahnuma Ahmed 向国家人权委员会提交酷刑指称投诉，是已发生的行动；该指称并非本项目独立核实的事实。

exactQuote: While in police custody Alam was allegedly subjected to torture, as detailed in submissions to the National Human Rights Commission filed by Alam’s wife.
explanation: 报告明确将国家人权委员会的相关提交归于 Alam 的妻子，酷刑保留为指称。

exactQuote: On these grounds, Alam filed a writ petition before the High Court challenging the continuation of the investigation against him, stating that such continuation not only contravened Section 61 of the DSA but also undermined his fundamental rights to equality, protection of law, fair trial and punishment, and freedom of speech guaranteed under Part III of the Bangladesh Constitution.
explanation: Alam 已向高等法院挑战继续调查的合法性；原文所列权利受损是其申请主张，不是法院全部采纳的结论。

exactQuote: On March 14, 2019, the High Court made an initial finding that the police did not have jurisdiction to continue to investigate the case due to the repeal of Section 57. The Court issued an interim order staying the investigation of the case for three months and ordered the government to prove that the investigation had lawful authority and was not outside the bounds of the DSA and the Constitution.
explanation: 2019-03-14 高等法院作出暂时中止调查三个月的命令；这不是撤销案件或无罪判决。

exactQuote: Alam subsequently filed a petition before the Appellate Division to challenge the High Court’s judgment. On November 27, 2022, the Appellate Division dismissed his petition.
explanation: Alam 向上诉庭挑战高等法院裁判，但 2022-11-27 申请被驳回；这是关于继续调查的程序，并不是对定罪的上诉。

exactQuote: The High Court’s decision in Alam’s case – and the Appellate Division’s recent dismissal of Alam’s appeal, with the result that the criminal investigation can proceed unfettered
explanation: 作者说明申请被驳回后刑事调查可继续；其后对公平性的批评属于作者评价。

exactQuote: TrialWatch, a Clooney Foundation for Justice (CFJ) initiative, has been monitoring the proceedings against Alam, who faces up to 14 years in prison.
explanation: TrialWatch 记录正在监测程序；最高可能刑罚不能记录成 Alam 已获的刑期。

exactQuote: Based on international standards, as paralleled by Indian precedent, the investigation against Alam should be quashed or discontinued.
explanation: 作者建议撤销或停止调查；报告没有把该建议记为已执行。

exactQuote: Ms. Andreyeva and Ms. Chultsova are both correspondents for Belsat TV, a Poland-based media outlet operating in Belarus. On November 15, 2020, they were assigned to cover a demonstration.
explanation: 报告将两人均记为 Belsat TV 通讯记者，2020-11-15 受派报道示威。

exactQuote: Ms. Andreyeva reported on the demonstration while Ms. Chultsova operated the camera.
explanation: 两人角色分别为现场报道和摄像，不能合并成同一个人。

exactQuote: Approximately five hours after the broadcast started, police officers burst through the door and arrested Ms. Andreyeva and Ms. Chultsova.
explanation: 报告记载警员闯入并逮捕两人；与同页示威日期一并读取。

exactQuote: Their trial started on February 9, 2021, before the Frunzensky District Court in Minsk, and ended on February 18 with their conviction.
explanation: 报告明确审判于 2021-02-09 开始，2 月 18 日定罪。

exactQuote: They were convicted and sentenced to two years in prison.
explanation: 两人的实际一审结果是定罪并各判两年监禁，不是最高可能刑期。

exactQuote: The court further denied defense requests to obtain official records of why traffic was stopped on the day of the protests and whether law enforcement had perhaps played a role.
explanation: 辩方请求取得为何停止交通的官方记录被法院拒绝；不是辩方已获得案卷。

exactQuote: Over the course of four hearings held in February 2021, the American Bar Association (ABA) Center for Human Rights and Human Rights Embassy monitored the trial of journalists Katsiaryna Andreyeva and Daria Chultsova in Belarus as part of the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s Trial Watch initiative.
explanation: ABA 人权中心和 Human Rights Embassy 实际监测四场听证，没有证据显示监测改变刑期。

exactQuote: On April 23, the Minsk Court of Appeals upheld the lower court’s verdict in full.
explanation: 报告正文记载上诉法院于 4 月 23 日维持原判，但本句没有年份；不将脚注新闻日期当成已核对的裁判日，结构化事件日期保留未知。

exactQuote: 288 Belsat, “‘No Miracle Happened’: Court upholds sentencing Belsat journos Katsyaryna Andreyeva, Daria Chultsova”, April 23, 2021.
explanation: 仅核对本报告脚注的书目标记：所引新闻列作 April 23, 2021。未获取所引新闻或原始裁判，不以此确认实际裁判年份或日期。

exactQuote: Current monitoring mechanisms, such as the ongoing Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights investigation and the International Accountability Platform, should highlight such violations as part of their documentation efforts.
explanation: 作者建议现有国际监测机制突出记录此类侵害；不是这些机制已经受理两人的个人申诉。

exactQuote: On January 12, 2025, Mzia Amaglobeli, 4 a renowned and award -winning Georgian journalist, was arrested on charges of “attacking a police officer in connection with their official duties” (Article 353 Prima of the Criminal Code of Georgia) after slapping a police chief during a protest in Batumi, Georgia.
explanation: 报告记录记者身份、2025-01-12 逮捕与抗议现场掌掴事件；法院指控及作者关于政治动机的评价须分开。

exactQuote: As discussed above, the defense also renewed its challenge to Mzia’s pretrial detention, calling it illegal and disproportionate, and announced the submission of an application challenging her pretrial detention to the European Court of Human Rights (“ECtH R”).
explanation: 辩方已再次挑战审前羁押，并宣布向欧洲人权法院提交申请；不等于该法院已受理、认定侵害或命令释放。

exactQuote: The judge granted continued detention, citing the threat of Mzia “commit[ting] a new criminal act.”
explanation: 在该次羁押挑战后，法官仍准许继续羁押；“可能再犯罪”是法官援引的理由。

exactQuote: On August 6, 2025, Judge Sakhelashvili found Mzia guilty but, without notice to the parties during the trial, downgraded the charge to a violation of Article 353(1) – a lesser offense that covers “resisting a police officer . . . with the aim of obstructin g the protection of public order, interrupting or altering [their activities],” punishable by a fine, house arrest for up to two years, or imprisonment for a term of two to five years.228 Mzia was sentenced to two years in prison.
explanation: 2025-08-06 法官在判决时改用较轻的“抗拒警察”罪名，并判两年监禁；罪名降低没有变成无罪或获释。

exactQuote: Both parties to the case filed appeals of the judgment of the Batumi City Court. The defense appeal sought acquittal, 231 while the prosecution sought to overturn the trial judgment and conviction on the initial charge of violating Article 353 Prima.
explanation: 双方都上诉：辩方求无罪，检方求恢复原始较重罪名。不要将检方请求写作辩方行动。

exactQuote: After deliberating for under an hour, the judges announced their decision, upholding the judgment of the Batumi City Court in full.
explanation: 上诉法院全面维持一审判决；该段没有明确日历日期，结构化结果保留月份级别。

exactQuote: The appeal hearings took place on November 11, 14, and 18, 2025, at the Kutaisi Court of Appeal with Judges Nikoloz Margvelashvili (the reporting judge), Nana Jokhadze, and Marina Siradze presiding.
explanation: 上诉听证于 2025 年 11 月三日举行；与维持原判段共同支持月份级别时间。

exactQuote: Mzia’s lawyers are submitting an appeal to the Supreme Court of Georgia.
explanation: 报告仅以进行时记录向最高法院提交上诉，没有记载该院受理或裁判结果。

exactQuote: CFJ deployed monitors to observe the trial of Mzia Amaglobeli in -person before the Batumi City Court and on appeal before the Kutaisi Court of Appeal. The monitors were fluent in Georgian.
explanation: CFJ 派会格鲁吉亚语的监测员现场观察一审及上诉；该段只证明实际监测，不证明改变结果。

exactQuote: Judgment of the Kutaisi Court of Appeal, issued on Nov. 18, 2025, (Case No. 010100125011054171) (hereinafter “Appeal Judgment”).
explanation: 仅核对本报告日期标记：脚注写 2025-11-18，方法部分另列 2025-12-02；报告未解释差异。未取得所引裁判，不确认实际签发日。

exactQuote: Judgment of the Kutaisi Court of Appeal (Dec. 2, 2025).
explanation: 仅核对本报告方法脚注写有 2025-12-02；与 PDF43 的日期标记差异保留。未取得所引裁判，不将该标记当作已证实的裁判日。

exactQuote: Mr. Zamora, known for his investigative journalism into government corruption, has been a beneficiary of precautionary measures from the Inter-American Commission for Human Rights (IACHR) for nearly two decades due to the threats he faced as a journalist.
explanation: 报告记载 Zamora 的调查新闻工作及长期面临威胁；有关保护措施仅作为该报告记载，不声称已复核措施原文。

exactQuote: On July 29, 2022, authorities conducted a raid on his house and arrested him on charges of money laundering, influence peddling, and blackmail based on a single complaint filed by a former banker who is under investigation for financial crimes.
explanation: 2022-07-29 的逮捕针对洗钱、影响力交易及勒索指控，指控不等于已证实行为。

exactQuote: His defense lawyers were repeatedly harassed, forcing him to change counsel multiple times (totaling ten lawyers by the end of the trial). Four of his lawyers were prosecuted and pressured into accepting the charges against them; a fifth reported facing intimidation and threats, and left the country. His lawyers faced difficulty accessing critical evidence and documents in a timely manner,
explanation: 报告记录律师多次更换、部分律师被起诉及取证困难。律师本人被起诉的结果不归到 Zamora 名下；作者“骚扰”的定性保留为作者描述。

exactQuote: On June 14, the presiding judge opened the hearing and declared the oral and debate period of the trial to be concluded.
explanation: 同章及脚注指向 2023-06-14 的宣判听证；与次页判项一起使用。

exactQuote: Mr. Zamora was convicted of money laundering and sentenced to six years in prison.
explanation: 这是 Zamora 的一审有罪判项和六年刑期，后被撤销；不能作为截至报告仍有效的最终判决。

exactQuote: Mr. Zamora was acquitted of the charges of blackmail and influence peddling.
explanation: Zamora 的一审无罪仅限勒索和影响力交易两项，后亦被撤销；共同被告 Gómez 的无罪另属一人。

exactQuote: In July 2023, the parties filed appeals: The Public Ministry filed two appeals (an appeal on formal grounds and a special appeal) requesting that the Appeals Court annul Mr. Zamora’s sentence and refer the case back to the trial court for a new debate and a new sentence, with different judges.240 Mr. Zamora’s defense counsel filed two appeals: 1. A special appeal on procedural grounds against the decision s made by the controlling judge in the evidentiary hearing, alleging a violation of the right to defense, based on: a) Preventing the defense from presenting exculpatory evidence in favor of the accused during the trial. b) The judge's authorization of the use of what they argued was illegal evidence against Mr. Zamora, specifically recordings of telephone conversations, made without authorization in Mr. Zamora’s home. The appeal asked for proceedings through the ‘offering of evidence’ hearing to be annulled so that the defense could present relevant evidence at trial.
explanation: 辩方实际在 2023 年 7 月提起上诉，要求撤销至证据提交阶段以补充辩护证据；同段检方提出的上诉不归作辩方行动。

exactQuote: 2. An appeal on the merits against the trial court for erroneous application of the law and violation of the principle of legality.
explanation: 第二项辩方上诉是针对法律适用及罪刑法定原则的实体争议，不是报告认为该请求已经获准。

exactQuote: On June 21, 2023, the IACHR and its Special Rapporteur for Freedom of Expression “expressed their grave concern” over the prison sentence handed to Mr. Zamora. 238 It reiterated the Rapporteur’s previous request (made in September 2022)239 for an on-site visit to verify Mr. Zamora’s situation.
explanation: 美洲人权委员会及言论自由特别报告员表达关切并重申现场探访请求；不是确认探访已发生。

exactQuote: On October 10, 2023, the Second Court of Appeals issued a decision based on the PGN’s special appeal. 245 It annulled the entire sentence: Mr. Zamora’s conviction for money laundering and his acquittals on the charges of blackmail and influence peddling . It also annulled the acquittal of Ms. Gómez. The Appeals Court ordered the case remanded to a new trial court, the Ninth Criminal Sentencing Court, for a new “debate” – that is, for a retrial beginning with the oral and debate stage of the proceedings . (This meant that Judge Orellana’s decisions in the proceedings through the evidentiary hearing would remain in place). The Appeals Court declined to consider Mr. Zamora’s appeals and the prosecutor’s appeals.
explanation: 上诉法院依国家总检察署的特别上诉撤销全部原判，并发回重审；Zamora 自己的上诉未被审议，不能归因于辩方上诉成功或写为最终无罪。

exactQuote: 245 Second Court of Appeals, Drug Trafficking and Environmental Crimes, No. 01079-2022-00280, Special Appeal 307-2023, October 20, 2023.
explanation: 仅核对本报告内部标记：脚注写 2023-10-20，正文写 2023-10-10。未独立调取所引原判，不确认哪一日是实际裁判日。

exactQuote: The retrial ordered by the Appeals Court is pending awaiting a cassation decision by the Criminal Chamber of the Supreme Court. In the meantime, Mr. Zamora has remained in detention as of the publication of this report in February 2024.
explanation: 报告明确：重审等待最高法院刑事庭审查决定，Zamora 截至 2024 年 2 月仍被羁押。

exactQuote: As part of the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative, the ABA Center for Human Rights deployed three monitors to proceedings before the Seventh Court of First Criminal Instance, Drug Trafficking and Environmental Crimes and before the Eighth Criminal Sentencing Court, Drug Trafficking and Environmental Crimes in Guatemala City. The monitors were fluent in Spanish and able to understand the proceedings. The Center observed the hearings on August 3, 8 and 9, 2022 via video feed and audio recordings. Monitors were deployed in-person to the hearings on December 8 and 22, 2022; May 2-4, 8-9, 10-11, 18-19, 22-23, and 30-31; and June 14, 2023.
explanation: ABA 人权中心以 TrialWatch 项目进行远程及现场监测；监测本身没有证明导致撤销判决或释放。

exactQuote: 1. Order the immediate release and dismissal of all charges against Mr. Zamora, acknowledging that the initial prosecution was unfounded and should not have occurred. However, if a retrial occurs, it must be conducted with strict adherence to international standards of due process and freedom of expression.
explanation: 作者建议立即释放并撤销全部指控，并为可能重审提出标准；这不是已经实施的措施。

exactQuote: Ms. Zolotova is the editor-in-chief of Tut.By, the largest independent online news portal in Belarus,3 a country dominated by state and state-affiliated media.
explanation: 报告明确其身份为 Tut.By 总编辑；不凭后来其他案件信息扩充此次报告。

exactQuote: In August 2018, Ms. Zolotova and at least 17 other journalists were arrested and detained on suspicion of sharing passwords to paywalled content from BeLTA, a state-run news agency: BeLTA imposed paywalls on its website articles for five to ten minutes, after which it granted public access.
explanation: 2018 年 8 月逮捕背景是涉嫌共享付费内容密码；“涉嫌”不能改成既定犯罪事实。

exactQuote: Following the investigation, the authorities dropped criminal charges against all journalists excepting Ms. Zolotova , imposing administrative fines instead. The prosecution of Ms. Zolotova, however, went forward.
explanation: 刑事指控被撤并改行政罚款的是其他记者；Zolotova 的起诉继续，不能串接为她已撤案。

exactQuote: According to Ms. Zolotova, she did not request counsel during her initial interrogation and was questioned without a lawyer.
explanation: 无律师在场的初次讯问是 Zolotova 自己的叙述，且报告说她当时没有请求律师；不改写为律师明确被拒绝进入。

exactQuote: The proceedings, held before the Zavodskiy Rayon District Court in Minsk ,24 lasted approximately two weeks, concluding on February 25, 2019 with Ms. Zolotova’s conviction and the imposition of a fine of approximately 3400 euros.
explanation: 报告记录 2019-02-25 定罪并罚款约 3400 欧元；前文最高五年监禁并非实际判罚。

exactQuote: In advance of the proceedings, the Center sent a letter notifying the court of the monitoring. The monitors did not experience any impediments in entering the courtroom.
explanation: ABA 人权中心先函告法院将开展监测，监测员进入法庭未遇阻；不能因此推断全部过程公开。

exactQuote: Hearings took place every day from February 12 to February 19 and the trial concluded with the announcement of the judgment on February 25. Monitors were present for the entirety of the proceedings excepting a closed session on February 18 (when witnesses’ personal phone communications were discussed).
explanation: 监测员观察审判，但未参加 2 月 18 日的闭门部分；保留覆盖范围。

exactQuote: The Zavodskiy Rayon District Court convicted Ms. Zolotova but has yet to publish its judgment.
explanation: 截至报告该段，法院尚未公开判决理由；不是尚未宣告定罪。

exactQuote: In the present case, th e court read out the guilty verdict and sentence on February 25, 2019, with no explanation of how it had reached its decision. It is now July 26, 2019.
explanation: 原文明确写当前日期为 2019-07-26，因此事实截至日期与封面出版月份分别保留。

exactQuote: While the coming elections are seemingly heightening the risks faced by independent media, they are also an opportunity for Belarus to chart a new course and ensure that outlets such as Tut. By can operate freely.
explanation: 作者呼吁白俄罗斯保障独立媒体自由运作；这是原则性建议，不是法院已撤销 Zolotova 定罪。

exactQuote: On July 6, 2020, a Russian military court convicted Svetlana Prokopyeva, a journalist, of “justifying terrorism” for a radio broadcast that commented critically on Russia’s repressive political climate and its effect on a teenager who detonated a bomb at a local office of Russia’s Federal Security Service in the city of Arkhangelsk.
explanation: 报告记载记者身份、广播评论背景和定罪；原文“压制性政治环境”等措辞属于作者对背景的描述。

exactQuote: On July 6, 2020, the court found Ms. Prokopyeva guilty 39 and imposed a fine of 500,000 rubles (approximately US $6,950).40 The laptop she used to write articles was confiscated as a tool of the crime for which she was convicted.
explanation: 实际刑罚为罚款 50 万卢布并没收所用电脑；不把前句检方请求的六年监禁记作判刑。

exactQuote: At the conclusion of the trial, the prosecutor recommended a sentence of six years in prison and a four-year ban on working as a journalist.
explanation: 六年监禁及四年记者工作禁令是检方求刑，不是法院实际宣判结果。

exactQuote: The defense presented four expert reports completed by seven experts in linguistics and psychology, all of whom concurred in their findings that Ms. Prokopyeva’s article did not contain expressions of support for terrorism.
explanation: 本页记录辩方提交四份专家报告、七名专家认为文章没有支持恐怖主义的表述；这是专家意见而非法院无罪认定。

exactQuote: Nevertheless, in its verdict, the court dismissed all four defense expert reports and disregarded the expert witnesses’ testimony,
explanation: 报告记载法院在判决中排除辩方报告并不采专家证词；不能将提交报告本身等同于证据被采纳。

exactQuote: Ms. Prokopyeva’s defense attorneys filed a motion for Ms. Yakotsuts and Ms. Baykova to testify at trial, arguing that their testimony was particularly important since the indictment largely relied on the conclusions in their report.
explanation: 律师要求控方专家 Yakotsuts 和 Baykova 出庭，因为起诉依赖其报告；这是已提出的请求。

exactQuote: The court denied the motion without explanation and similarly refused the defense’s subsequent motion to exclude the report from evidence.
explanation: 法院拒绝传唤专家，也拒绝其后排除该报告的请求；不构成辩方程序胜利。

exactQuote: Following a successful petition by defense counsel, the remaining hearings were broadcast live on YouTube.
explanation: 辩方申请成功后，其余听证进行直播；这一局部公开程序变化没有使定罪消失。

exactQuote: The Clooney Foundation for Justice monitored this case through audio and video recordings of each hearing. The monitor, who speaks Russian, listened to audio recordings of the first three hearings.
explanation: CFJ 以录音及录像监測，前三场听录音，后续利用直播；不是声称全程现场旁听。

exactQuote: The authors of all three defense reports were allowed to testify at trial.
explanation: 此段称“三份”辩方报告作者均可作证，而 PDF13 称“四份”；保留计数差异，行动描述不用确定份数。

exactQuote: Bao Choy Yuk-ling (“Bao Choy”) is an award -winning 37-year-old investigative journalist and documentary film producer in Hong Kong. In the fall of 2019, she worked with RTHK to produce a documentary for its show “Hong Kong Connection” on the attacks against pro- democracy activists and other commuters at the Yuen Long metro station on July 21, 2019.81
explanation: 报告直接记载Bao Choy的调查记者身份及元朗事件纪录片背景。

exactQuote: The Defense argued that the Prosecution had failed to prove beyond reasonable doubt the three essential elements of the offense, namely that the Defendant’s statements were 1) “knowingly” made, 2) about a “material particular” and 3) “false.” The Defense first argued that the defendant did not “kno wingly” make a false statement as the terms used in the online form (e.g., “activities relating to traffic and transport matters”) are general and vague and so should be given the broadest interpretation . They also noted that no law or statute gives the Co mmissioner for Transport the authority to limit the purposes for which an information search through the public database is conducted.
explanation: 报告记载辩方争辩检方未证明知情、实质事项与虚假三个要件，并质疑表格用语和限制搜索用途的权限。这是已提出的抗辩，不代表获法院接受。

exactQuote: On April 22, 2021, the Principal Magistrate hearing the case found Bao Choy guilty on both counts of “knowingly making a false statement.” The Court observed that the Defendant’s statements on the online form were “false” because she had no need of the information for litigation or another valid rationale; her purpose, the Court said, was rather “to obtain the name and address of the registered owner of the Vehicle in order to conduct interviews and reporting, which had no connection with ‘other traffic and transport related matters.’”95 The Court ordered Bao Choy to pay a fine of HK $3,000 for each count for a total of HK $6,000 (in USD, approximately $775).
explanation: 报告记载2021年4月22日Bao Choy两项罪名成立及合计港币6,000元罚款，不能视为无罪或撤案。

exactQuote: On May 5, 2021, Bao Choy announced that she had submitted an appeal.96
explanation: 2021年5月5日是Bao Choy宣布已递交上诉的日期；报告未给出其后裁决。

exactQuote: This case appears to be the first prosecution of this kind under the Road Traffic Ordinance and resulted in Bao Choy’s conviction and a fine. Her appeal is pending.
explanation: 报告截至发布时仍将Bao Choy的上诉列为未决；不是当前案件状态。

exactQuote: TrialWatch monitored the one-day trial on March 24, 2021, and the delivery of the verdict on April 2 2, 2021. The proceedings took place in Cantonese at the West Kowloon Magistrates’ Court.
explanation: TrialWatch记载已观察2021年3月24日庭审和4月22日宣判。原提取文本将22断为“2 2”，保留原文。

exactQuote: First, the defendant was convicted of obscure charges simply for how she filled out an online form, routinely used by journalists and others without penalty; as such, the charges and prosecution give rise to concerns under the principle of legality. Second, given the context in which this case emerged and indeed, the decisi on to drop similar charges against a pro -government reporter after this case was decided, the prosecution raises concerns that it was an abuse of process, brought selectively and with improper motives to chill exercise of free expression, a protected right under international and Hong Kong law. These concerns can and should be resolved on appeal.
explanation: 专家认为上述疑虑可以且应在上诉中解决；这是作者建议，不是已发生的上诉结果。

exactQuote: From July 2020 to February 2021 , the Clooney Foundation for Justice monitored contempt of court proceedings against the news outlet Malaysiakini and its editor-in-chief Steven Gan . The defendants were accused of contempt of court on the basis of unmoderated subscriber comments on a Malaysiakini article about an order by the Malaysian Federal Court’s Chief Justice to reopen courts following their closure because of the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the prosecution, the comments, which criticized various courts and judges for corruption and incompetence, were insulting to the judiciary.
explanation: 报告将本案界定为针对新闻机构和总编辑的读者评论藐视法庭程序。

exactQuote: All were posted under pseudonyms.106 Malaysiakini was not aware of the comments until informed by police.107 It removed them twelve minutes later and banned the five users who posted them.108 These facts were not contested by the prosecution. Malaysiakini agreed that the comments were offensive and inappropriate and apologized for indirectly allowing the comments to be published.109
explanation: 报告记载警方通知后12分钟删除评论、封禁用户并致歉；不据此推断法院免除责任。

exactQuote: The defense also argued that Malaysiakini’s compliance with the Malaysia Communications and Multimedia Content Code (MCMC Code) obviated any liability. According to the defense, the MCMC Code did not require websites to monitor comments and allowed a two-day window to take down posts.132 On February 19, 2021, the Federal Court found Malaysiakini guilty of contempt and acquitted editor-in-chief Steven Gan.
explanation: 辩方援引内容准则；报告随后明确区分2021年2月19日Malaysiakini被定罪与Steven Gan无罪。

exactQuote: The court thus stated that “[p]ublic interest demand [ed] a deterrent sentence be meted out against the First Respondent,” imposing a fine of RM 500,000 (approximately $118,000 USD).152
explanation: 联邦法院对Malaysiakini判处RM 500,000罚款；这不是Steven Gan个人罚款。

exactQuote: Within hours of the verdict, Malaysiakini had raised enough via crowdfunding to pay the entirety of the RM 500,000 fine.155
explanation: 报告记载Malaysiakini在判决后数小时内筹得足以支付全额罚款的资金；筹资不等于撤销定罪。

exactQuote: Although there is no higher court than the Federal Court, meaning that Malaysiakini could not appeal the conviction, it is possible to seek review of a decision by the Federal Court. In May, Malaysiakini sought such a review so as to set aside its contempt conviction. The Federal Court has scheduled the review hearing for October 12.
explanation: 报告区分普通上诉与联邦法院复核，并记载Malaysiakini于5月申请复核、听证预定10月12日。

exactQuote: The Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch Initiative deployed monitors to both the hearing on the merits on July 13, 2020 before the Federal Court and the court’s issuance of the verdict on February 19, 2021. The monitors were fluent in Malay and did not experience any impediments in entering the courtroom. The monitors used the CFJ TrialWatch App to record and track what transpired in court and the degree to which the defendants’ fair trial rights were respected.
explanation: TrialWatch部署会马来语的观察员参加实体听证及宣判并记录程序。

exactQuote: In light of the above, on October 12 the Federal Court should set aside Malaysiakini’s conviction.
explanation: 报告呼吁联邦法院于10月12日复核时撤销Malaysiakini定罪；这是建议，不是复核结果。

exactQuote: Ms. Raissouni is a journalist for Akhbar Al Yaoum , an independent news outlet. Akhbar Al Yaoum is one of Morocco’s few remaining newspapers critical of the government, and the government has taken several measures against it since the newspaper’s creation in 2009.1
explanation: 报告识别Hajar Raissouni为独立报纸记者，并描述媒体背景；不据此自行判定起诉动机。

exactQuote: Following their detention and interrogation, Ms. Raissouni and her co -defendants were charged on September 2, 2019. They were kept in pre -trial detention, despite attempts to procure bail, through to their convictions on September 30, 2019.
explanation: 报告记载2019年9月2日起诉后，共同被告虽尝试获得保释，仍被羁押至9月30日定罪；未提供每次申请日期。

exactQuote: De fense counsel also offered to submit documentary evidence to support the claimed reasons the marriage had not yet been registered,32 and sought to have the witnesses to Ms. Raissouni’s religious marriage and the doctor who performed the medical examination called to testify, 33 but the judge refused.34
explanation: 辩方提出补充书面材料并申请相关证人作证，法官拒绝。仅记录程序性申请，不重述非必要私人生活细节。

exactQuote: On September 30, 2019, all five defendants were found guilty, and Ms. Raissouni and her fiancé were each sentenced to one year in prison and fined, Dr. Belkeziz was sentenced to two years in prison and fined, and Mr. Baba and Ms. Azelmadh were given suspended sentences of eight months and fined.
explanation: 报告分别记载Hajar Raissouni和未婚夫一年监禁、医生两年监禁、其余两名共同被告八个月缓刑，均有罚款。不得把不同被告刑罚合并。

exactQuote: Ultimately, on October 16, 2019, the King of Morocco pardoned all five defendants.
explanation: 报告记载国王于2019年10月16日赦免五名被告；本摘录本身不证明赦免由何种倡导行动造成。

exactQuote: Moreover, a pardon is not an acquittal on the merits
explanation: 报告明确区分赦免与实体无罪判决，避免把免服刑解读为指控已被事实推翻。

exactQuote: As part of the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative, the Clooney Foundation for Justice deployed monitors, who were assisted by Arabic translators, to attend Ms. Raissouni’s trial in Morocco. Though one monitor experienced temporary imp ediments to entering the courtroom, ultimately monitors were able to attend the two substantive hearings as well as the delivery of the judgment. However, given the quality of the sound system, the number of people in the courtroom, and other conditions, there were many instances where the monitor and translator were unable to hear the examinations of the defendants and thus were unable to completely capture the content of their statements. In many cases, the testimony was, however, summarized in the Judgment.
explanation: TrialWatch观察两次实体听证及宣判；报告也说明声音及现场条件造成记录缺失，不能视为全程完整逐字记录。

exactQuote: At a minimum, Ms. Raissouni’s trial was marred by the appearance of judicial bias. For instance, the court credited evidence obtained in violation of Moroccan law and , even then, convicted the defendants without sufficient evidence to substantiate the char ges. The court also interfered with Ms. Raissouni’s ability to put on a defense by preventing her from calling witnesses and offering other potentially relevant evidence.
explanation: 报告作者认为存在司法偏见外观、证据不足和限制辩方举证等问题；这是作者评估，不是后续法院撤销裁决。

exactQuote: Omar Radi is an award-winning Moroccan investigative journalist and activist.37 He is one of the only journalists to have closely monitored the financial holdings of the King of Morocco.38 Mr. Radi has carried out his work as a journalist in Morocco in spite of repeated denials by the Moroccan government of his applications for a press pass, often on the pretext that they could not find the necessary documents in his applications to issue one.39 (Mr. Radi was ultimately issued a press pass several months after the trial.) The case against Mr. Radi stemmed from a tweet he posted on Twitter on April 6, 2019.40
explanation: 报告确认Omar Radi调查记者及活动人士身份，并把该程序追溯至2019年4月6日推文。

exactQuote: Mr. Radi’s attorneys requested bail, but the presiding judge denied the request. The next day, Mr. Radi’s attorneys appealed the bail decision and an appeal hearing was held on the same day. On December 31, 2019, the appeal court granted Mr. Radi bail.
explanation: 律师在保释被拒后于次日提出上诉，报告记载2019年12月31日准予保释。

exactQuote: Mr. Radi’s trial was originally scheduled for January 2, 2020, but Mr. Radi’s attorneys applied for an extension t o prepare their defense, and it was granted. The judge scheduled the trial for March 5, 2020.
explanation: 辩方请求延期开庭以准备辩护，获准后庭期改为2020年3月5日；申请日未单列。

exactQuote: On March 17, 2020, the trial judge convicted Mr. Radi and gave him a four -month suspended sentence and 500 Dirham fine.56 Mr. Radi’s lawyer filed a notice of appeal of the judgment in court that day.57
explanation: 报告记载Omar Radi于2020年3月17日被判四个月缓刑及500迪拉姆罚款，律师同日提交上诉通知；不是无罪。

exactQuote: Mr. Radi’s three lawyers then began their oral arguments. The first lawyer argued that Mr. Radi was not arrested for his tweet, but instead for his investigation of public servants, which disclosed inconsistencies in the Moroccan government’s budget. He was also the first one to investigate issues surrounding the state’s distribution of free lands to state agents. The lawyer then emphasized that the Moroccan Constitution guaranteed Mr. Radi’s right to freedom of expression. He further argued that by using the word “bourreau” Mr. Radi meant “the shockingly unexpected sentences against innocent activists.”54 The second lawyer stressed that the government hindered Mr. Radi’s journalism by repeatedly denying him a press pass and losing Mr. Radi’s documents when he requested one. He also highlighted that it was unreasonable to prosecute a journalist under the Penal Code when the Press Code exists. Lastly, he stressed that Mr. Radi had tweeted eight months before his arrest.
explanation: 报告记载辩方就新闻调查背景、宪法表达保障、推文含义及刑法与新闻法的适用进行抗辩。

exactQuote: USC’s International Human Rights Clinic, as part of the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative, deployed two local monitors in Morocco to observe the proceedings against Omar Radi. Prior to the trial, background research, including preparation of the monitors, was undertaken. The monitors did not experience any impediments in entering the courtroom and were present for the trial on March 5, 2020.
explanation: USC国际人权诊所部署两名本地观察员参加2020年3月5日庭审。

exactQuote: As recommended by the UN Human Rights Committee, and in advance of Morocco’s seventh reporting cycle to the UN Human Rights Committee beginning in November 2020 with its State Party Report, Morocco should consider revising its Penal Code to address concerns regarding the protection of freedom of expression and to ensure congruence with the new Press Code.
explanation: 作者呼吁摩洛哥考虑修订刑法，以回应表达自由保障及与新新闻法一致性问题；不是已实施改革。

exactQuote: As part of the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative, the USC Gould School of Law International Human Rights Clinic monitored the trial of Moroccan journalist Omar Radi, which concluded on July 19, 2021, as well as the subsequent appeal, which concluded on March 3, 2022. Omar Radi is an investigative journalist who has reported on government corruption, including the financial holdings of the Moroccan monarchy, since 2008.
explanation: 报告明确USC观察本次一审及上诉，并识别Omar Radi的调查记者身份；本案终点分别为2021年7月19日与2022年3月3日。

exactQuote: Ultimately, on July 29, 2020, the government arrested Mr. Radi and charged him with four crimes: undermining the internal security of the State; undermining the external security of the State; indecent assault; and, rape.
explanation: 报告记载2020年7月29日逮捕及四项指控；所列为控罪，不能把指控本身表述为已独立证实的行为。

exactQuote: Multiple requests were made throughout the pre-trial process and during trial for Mr. Radi’s release, all of which were denied.97
explanation: 报告记载审前及审判期间多次请求释放均遭拒；没有单列所有请求的提交日。

exactQuote: On July 19, 2021, Mr. Radi was convicted on all counts and sentenced to six years in prison. He was also required to compensate the complainant 200,000 Moroccan Dirhams in damages.2
explanation: 报告记载Omar Radi于2021年7月19日所有控罪成立、六年监禁及赔偿要求；结果仅属于本次程序。

exactQuote: Shortly after the conviction, Mr. Radi appealed the decision. Although the appeal was scheduled to begin on November 4, 2021, it was postponed several times and began in January 2022. On March 3, 2022, the Court of Appeals affirmed Mr. Radi’s conviction. During the appeal hearings, the court again denied Mr. Radi the opportunity to call his own exculpatory witness or cross-examine the key prosecution witness.
explanation: 摘要记载上诉维持及证人问题，并称上诉于2022年1月开始；与正文第26页的延期时间表存在差异，未自行消除。

exactQuote: Following his conviction, Mr. Radi’s lawyers promptly filed an appeal. 202 Mr. Radi was denied release pending the appeal. 203 An appeal hearing was originally scheduled for November 4, 2021, but post poned eight times until February 15, 2022. 204 On March 3, 2022, the Appeals Court in Casablanca upheld the first instance conviction of Mr. Radi, confirming his six-year sentence for espionage and rape.205
explanation: 正文记载律师上诉、候审释放被拒，以及2022年3月3日维持六年刑期；开庭延期表述与摘要存在差异。

exactQuote: Mr. Radi’s defense counsel raised his health condition during the hearing on June 1, 2021, and the judge authorized Mr. Radi to make a statement.
explanation: 2021年6月1日辩护律师在庭上提出健康问题，法官准许Omar Radi陈述；不把准许陈述当作健康待遇已经改善。

exactQuote: In sum, the treatment of and proceedings against Mr. Radi entailed violations of his right to the presumption of innocence, right not to be arbitrarily detained or subjected to inhumane treatment, right to call and examine witnesses, and right to an impartial tribunal. Furthermore, this case is situated within the context of Morocco’s ongoing pattern of using a wide variety of laws, including sex-related crimes, to tar the reputation of journalists and dissidents. Speaking out against the Palace, such as by exposing alleged corruption as relates to the monarchy’s financial ho ldings, appears to have dire consequences. For these reasons, this report finds that the proceedings against Mr. Radi constituted an abuse of process.
explanation: 报告结论是作者对程序公正及滥用程序的评估，不是无罪裁判或指控事实的独立核实。

exactQuote: Between March and May 2019, TrialWatch monitors under the supervision of the Columbia Law School Human Rights Clinic monitored the trial of Cansu Pişkin, a journalist for the Turkish daily paper, Evrensel, in Istanbul, Turkey. Pişkin was charged with “making a public servant into a target for terrorist organizations” in violation of Section 6(1) of Law No. 3713, otherwise known as the Anti-Terror Law, for publishing the prosecutor’s name in her April 5, 2018 article, “Special Prosecutor for the Bosphorus Students.”
explanation: 报告识别Cansu Pişkin为Evrensel记者，并说明被诉源于2018年4月5日文章中的检察官姓名。

exactQuote: An attorney for Cansu Pişkin began the hearing by arguing that the case should be dropped for lack of jurisdiction. Although the case was brought under the Anti-Terror Law, defense counsel argued that Turkey’s Press Law29 (which generally governs criminal cases brought on the basis of journalistic material) limited the prosecution’s ability to file charges based on articles published online where the statute of limitations had passed. He noted that a high court in Ankara had also found it lacked jurisdiction over a case where the statute of limitations had run before the charges were brought (based on when the article was published) and noted that given this precedent and the fact that the charges were not brought promptly against Pişkin, the charges should be dropped.30 The court briefly had the courtroom vacated to consider the argument then reconvened and informed the parties and the audience that because the article was published online, the charges had been brought in a timely matter and the prosecution would continue.
explanation: 辩护律师提出管辖及起诉时效异议，法院讨论后仍决定继续起诉；这是实际采取但未成功终结程序的抗辩。

exactQuote: Pişkin and her attorneys maintained that she included the name of the prosecutor in her article because the identity of the prosecutor was newsworthy, not with any criminal intent. In particular, Pişkin noted (a) the fact that the investigation’s prosecutor was changed on the day that Boğaziçi students were brought to the court was newsworthy, especially given the public interest in the case and the students’ long pre-trial detention; and (b) that this prosecutor had previously defined the People’s Democratic Party (HDP) as a political party that acts under directions from a terrorist organization, a remark that conflicts with a prosecutor’s professional principles. Pişkin’s attorneys argued both that she had no criminal intent to make the prosecutor a target and also that the name of the prosecutor had been previously published by other media outlets with no ramifications for the other journalists. Further, the attorneys argued that a Public Prosecutor is not a public official under Article 6(1) of the Anti-Terror Law so the charges should be dismissed.
explanation: 辩方提出无犯罪故意、姓名此前已公开以及检察官是否属于法条涵盖人员等论点。

exactQuote: The Court then found Pişkin guilty of the terrorism charge (“making a public servant into a target for terrorist organizations”) and sentenced her to ten months’ imprisonment. The sentence imposition was deferred, pursuant to Article 231(11) of the Criminal Code of Procedure, whereby Pişkin will be subject to five years of monitoring and will not be imprisoned unless she “deliberately commits a crime within the monitoring period.”34
explanation: 报告记载十个月刑期被延缓并设置五年监督；不能只引用监禁数字就声称Pişkin已被投入监狱。

exactQuote: The Columbia Law School Human Rights Clinic or their local partners monitored all three hearings. In advance of monitoring mission, the Clinic informed one of the defense attorneys of its intention to monitor the case and procured the charge sheet from local advocates also following the case. The Clinic prepared a background memorandum for the monitors outlining key information on human rights and freedom of expression in Turkey, the judicial system and laws at issue in this case, the right to a fair trial under Turkish law, and laws impacting freedom of expression and national security laws in Turkey. This report also included information on the trial, including the charges against the defendant and the facts of the case. None of the monitors experienced any impediments to their entry into the courtroom. The Columbia team provided a letter of accreditation to the Court. In the first hearing, the Columbia monitors were accompanied by a professional interpreter who was permitted to provide whisper translation to the team during the proceedings. The Columbia team worked with professional interpreters to translate the indictment and court transcripts, included in this report as Annexes. All monitors used a standardized TrialWatch questionnaire to record and track what transpired in court and the degree to which the defendant’s fair trial rights were respected in the proceedings.
explanation: 哥伦比亚团队或当地伙伴观察三次听证，向法院提供认证函，并安排口译、材料翻译与标准化记录。

exactQuote: While the trial of Cansu Pişkin was conducted in a manner that appeared to accord her certain of her rights as an accused person in a criminal trial, the prosecution of the case must be seen as a politically-motivated response to her publication, which called into question the independence of the prosecution of students who had peacefully protested the Turkish military incursion into Afrin, Syria. Additionally, the trial itself was defective in that an element of the charge—namely, the specific intent to target an individual to a terrorist threat—was not proved, and in having resulted in a disposition that further restricted her right to free expression. I would assign a grade of D based upon significant violations of the right of trial fairness, while not assigning a failing grade because the proceedings did not result in the imprisonment of the accused person.
explanation: 作者批评程序公平性，但明确指出本程序未导致Cansu Pişkin实际入狱；此项不代表无罪。

exactQuote: For instance, journalist Asad Ali Toor tweeted about alleged corruption by a former army officer and then-government official, saying “I read whatever I see with an open mind and would also request you in this country nobody is holy cow & must not be above the law, I’m journalist with bias for democracy/constitution/rule of law. If our all other segments of society are answerable/accountable why not Asim Bajwa?”. 41 Soon thereafter, a private person filed an FIR alleging that “[i]n the last few days, Mr. Toor has used derogatory language and negative propaganda for high -level government institutions, including the Pakistan Army through his social media posts which is a grave crime according to t he law.”42
explanation: 报告把记者身份、相关推文和私人投诉联系起来；投诉指控不是已证实犯罪。

exactQuote: Ultimately, Mr. Toor moved to quash the FIR before the Lahore High Court. He explained that the FIR did not “disclose[] any particulars of the Twitter account or internet device through which the complainant accessed the allegedly defamatory tweets. He has not, for instance, mentioned whether he saw the allegedly defamatory tweets on his laptop or on his android? . . . The absence of such information which would establish the link between the Complainant and allegedly defamatory tweets strongly suggests that the Complainant is not the aggrieved person, he is only acting as a proxy.”45
explanation: Toor 向拉合尔高等法院申请撤销 FIR，质疑投诉者与相关推文的关联。

exactQuote: The case was ultimately closed by investigators (the investigators told the Lahore High Court that “no evidence has been collected against the petitioner revealing the commission of any offense”46).
explanation: 报告记载调查机关以未搜集到犯罪证据结案；不是法院无罪判决，也未证明诉讼单独造成结案。

exactQuote: Then, after he publicly asser ted that the authorities may have been behind the attack, a second private person lodged a fresh complaint against him.48 As Mr. Toor explained, “a private citizen got up and went for the report to the FIA. He claimed that I had conspired against the orga nizations, the Army, and the ISI and had accused them.”49 In this case, the FIA’s notice to appear specifically alleged “defamation of institution of Government of Pakistan through social media.” 50 This notice too , did not specify the allegedly offending speech, with the notice simply saying that “you are well aware of the facts/circumstances of the said inquiry.”51
explanation: 最初结案后另有私人投诉及含糊传唤；不能视为同一次程序。

exactQuote: The proceedings initiated by these notices were not pursued by the FIA after the notices were challenged in court – further suggesting that the case had not been an effort to vindicate the rights of a ‘natural person’ but rather in response to his criticism of the government.
explanation: 报告记载传唤被法院挑战后 FIA 未继续推进；末尾动机判断属于报告分析，不是法院事实认定。

exactQuote: Section 20 should be reformed. In the event Section 20 is not reformed or repealed, the government should concede it is unconstitutional. Further, the FIA should implement the Islamabad High Court’s order in the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists case to report on FIA abuses, which would also provide a basis for further action by bodies in Pakistan considering PECA’s Section 20.
explanation: 作者提出制度改革和报告 FIA 滥用情况的建议；未记录该建议已执行或带来个案结果。

exactQuote: Journalist Bilal Ghauri, for instance, received a WhatsApp message from an unknown number indicating that “FIA, Cyber Crime Reporting Center in Islamabad is conducting proceedings regarding defamation and harassment on the above cited enquiry. Reportedly you are well aware of the facts/circumstances of the subject matter.” 59
explanation: 报告记载记者经 WhatsApp 收到缺乏具体事实的传唤；未据此推断已被拘押。

exactQuote: When he responded requesting details, he was simply told the identity of the complainant and that it apparently related to YouTube. Indeed, he received a second notice that reiterated, “you must be well acquainted with the facts of the inquiry.” 60
explanation: Ghauri 询问细节后只获投诉人身份及与 YouTube 相关的模糊说明；后续通知仍未解释。

exactQuote: Mr. Ghauri took the notices to the Islamabad High Court, arguing that the first notice “did not disclose the offense” and arguing that the fact that the notice had been “sent through WhatsApp” “illustrates the mala fide within which the notice was issued.” 62 Mr. Ghauri’s counsel argued that the notices were “part of a campaign of silencing journalists.” 63
explanation: 当事人及律师向高等法院挑战传唤及送达方式；“压制记者运动”是律师论点。

exactQuote: Ultimately, the Islamabad High Court declared the case a nullity in the order finding Section 20 unconstitutional, and the notices were thus quashed.
explanation: 作者记载法院宣告程序无效并撤销传唤；不外推为今日一般法律状态。

exactQuote: Section 20 should be reformed. In the event Section 20 is not reformed or repealed, the government should concede it is unconstitutional. Further, the FIA should implement the Islamabad High Court’s order in the Pakistan Federal Union of Journalists case to report on FIA abuses, which would also provide a basis for further action by bodies in Pakistan considering PECA’s Section 20.
explanation: 主题报告的制度改革建议，未记录 Ghauri 个案因此得到进一步结果。

exactQuote: From May to August 2020, the American Bar Association (ABA) Center for Human Rights monitored criminal proceedings against journalist and filmmaker Moses Bwayo in Uganda as part of the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative . Mr. Bwayo was charged with unlawful assembly for shooting a scene for a documentary about opposition activist, presidential candidate, and musician Bobi Wine: the authorities alleged that the gathering and filming constituted subversion of the Ugandan government.
explanation: 报告明确其记者和电影制作者身份、纪录片活动、非法集会指控及庭审观察；指控并非犯罪事实认定。

exactQuote: Mr. Bwayo and the rest of the group were held for two days (until February 26), at which point they were released on police bond.59 They were instructed to report back to the police station a week later, on March 4.60 Having complied with these instructions, they were re-arrested and taken to the Chief Magistrate’s Court in Makindye,61 where they appeared before a judge, were formally charged, and made a bail application through their attorneys.62 The group was remanded to Luzira Prison until March 6, when the court granted bail.63
explanation: 报告分列警方保证释放、再次被捕、律师保释申请和3月6日法院准予保释。

exactQuote: Mr. Bwayo and the rest of the accused appeared in court on August 10 for trial.68 However, no witnesses for the prosecution appeared.69 The court declined the state attorney’s request for an adjournment, dismissing the case for lack of evidence.70 The court noted that the State appeared to lack sufficient interest in the matter and was imposing unnecessary costs on the accused.71
explanation: 8月10日无检方证人出庭，法院拒绝延期并因缺乏证据撤案；未把结果归因于保释或观察。

exactQuote: In the present case, Mr. Bwayo was detained for two days without access to counsel - from February 24 to February 26 - before being released on bond.81 During this time, he was interrogated: his witness statement, part of the case file introduced by the prosecution on June 5, was taken on February 25.82 According to credible sources on the ground, Mr. Bwayo requested a lawyer.
explanation: 正文记载被拘押两天且无法接触律师、期间受讯问，并注明其请求律师的消息来源；未另行核验这些底层材料。

exactQuote: Indeed, not three months after his criminal case was dismissed, Moses Bwayo was shot in the face by a police officer while covering the Bobi Wine campaign.
explanation: 报告记载撤案后采访期间遭枪击；这是后续安全事件，不改变已记录的撤案结果。

exactQuote: Uganda must commit to protecting - not obstructing - journalists reporting on the elections, in line with international and regional standards on freedom of expression and press freedom.
explanation: 作者要求保护选举报道记者；这是建议，不是已落实的保护措施。

exactQuote: In 2019, Samak Donnapee, a retired forestry officer, and Wuth Boonlert, an indigenous human rights advocate, were prosecuted and tried for criminal defamation. The charges, brought by a government officer, Chaiwat Limlikhit-aksorn, (in his private capacity) and the Public Prosecutor, relate to Facebook posts by Samak Donnapee.
explanation: 同案两人身份不同，指控涉及 Samak 的原帖；不将二人都标为记者。

exactQuote: Wuth Boonlert was accused of sharing one of these posts with no further commentary. None of the posts named Chaiwat Limlikhit-aksorn.
explanation: Wuth 被控无评论转发，报告称帖子未指名共同原告。

exactQuote: The trial of Samak Donnapee and Wuth Boonlert took place at Min Buri Criminal Court in Bangkok, Thailand, on September 10 and 11, 2019. The first day, September 10, centered on the examination of prosecution witnesses ; on the second day, the two defendants presented their defense. Samak Donnapee and Wuth Boonlert were tried together but Samak Donnapee represented himself and Wuth Boonlert was represented by attorneys from Cross Cultural Foundation.
explanation: 记录两天审判、Samak 自行辩护和 Wuth 的律师代理。

exactQuote: From approximately 11am to 1pm, Samak Donnapee presented himself as his own defense witness, with the judge questioning him as he read through his prepared testimony. Samak Donnapee began by explaining his history of service in the park office and how he felt it was his mission to expose corruption in the park department. He went on to explain that s ince his retirement in particular, he has used his Facebook p age to post about the forest and related issues, including land rights. Samak Donnapee then appeared to argue that truth was a defense to the alleged defamation, testifying that the Facebook posts were factual as they were based on government reports showing that the property encroached on the forest land. He also pointed out that they were about the Co- Plaintiff’s brother, as only he was named in the posts.
explanation: Samak 以本人证词说明公开资料依据并主张真实抗辩；这些是辩护主张，不等于报告证实全部指控。

exactQuote: After lunch, the case resumed with defendant Wuth Boonlert on the stand. Wuth Boonlert testified that he is a farmer and also works for a commission set up by the government to look into the cultural and economic issues of minority communities, including the Karen and other forest-dwelling communities. Wuth Boonlert further testified that he had never met the other defendant, Samak Donnapee , before the court proceedings but that he followed Samak Donnapee on Facebook because of their shared interest in forest issues and land rights. Wuth Boonlert testified that he shared Samak Donnapee’s August 28, 2016 post on his own Facebook page, without further commentary and making clear that it was Donnapee’s post, both to give Donnapee credit and also to convey that he wasn't saying the allegation was true but rather wanted to show its provenance and encourage the government to investigate.
explanation: Wuth 解释转发来源和目的，并非承认其转发中的指控为真。

exactQuote: November 18, 2019: Judgment The TrialWatch monitor and their interpreter attended the judgment on November 18, 2019 at 9:00am; both defendants were present, but the Co-Plaintiff was not. The Court found both defendants not guilty on all charges and thus declined the Co- Plaintiff’s request for damages.
explanation: 判决日两人所有指控均获无罪，法院同时拒绝共同原告损害赔偿请求。

exactQuote: Had either the Public Prosecutor or the Court conducted an appropriate, early examination of the Facebook posts in question, they should have been able to dismiss the matter without a full-blown trial.
explanation: 作者认为应尽早审查并避免完整审判；这是回顾性制度建议，不是已发生的庭前撤案。

exactQuote: From June 12 to June 22, 2020, the American Bar Association Center for Human Rights monitored the trial of Alnur Ilyashev in Kazakhstan as part of the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative. Ilyashev is a human rights activist and blogger. He was prosecuted under Article 274 of Kazakhstan’s Criminal Code for “disseminat[ing] knowingly false information” in a state of emergency on the basis of three Facebook posts that criticized the ruling Nur Otan party for corruption and incompetence, including in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The proceedings – held over videoconference because of COVID-19 – were marred by grave violations of Ilyashev’s right to a fair trial.
explanation: 报告明确活动者和博主身份、三则帖文与远程审判；严重违反公正审判的说法属于报告评价。

exactQuote: At closing, the prosecution requested that Ilyashev be sentenced to three years in prison and be banned from political and civic activism for five years.53 On June 22, Judge Makharadze sentenced Ilyashev to three years of restricted movement, including regular check-ins with a probation officer, and a five-year ban on political and civic activism.54 Ilyashev appealed his conviction.
explanation: 区分检方要求监禁与实际限制行动判决，并记录提出上诉。

exactQuote: Although the Almaty City Court – the appellate court – allowed the presentation of further evidence, on September 15 it upheld the lower court’s decision in full.55 The Kazakh Supreme Court recently denied Ilyashev’s appeal, finding that the court of first instance had sufficiently examined all relevant evidence. The defense has petitioned Kazakhstan’s Attorney General to “file a protest” with the Supreme Court requesting reconsideration of this decision.
explanation: 上诉法院维持原判、最高法院未准上诉与请求总检察长抗诉是三个不同步骤；最后一项结果未载明。

exactQuote: Consistent with the UN Human Rights Committee’s finding that courts must undertake periodic re-evaluation of whether detention remains necessary,72 Ilyashev made several requests for release prior to trial. All were denied by the Medeu court.
explanation: 正文明确审前多次释放请求均被拒；并非成功保释案例。

exactQuote: At the June 18 hearing, the defense noted that the two-month detention period initially approved by the court had expired, arguing that Ilyashev should be released and offering to post bail.78 In denying the request, the court stated that the maximum possible time for pretrial detention was six months, and thus Ilyashev could remain in pretrial detention for that entire period.79
explanation: 辩方在庭审中以最初拘押期已满要求释放并提出保释，法院拒绝。

exactQuote: With respect to the confidentiality of the communications, Ilyashev was restricted to discussing the case with his lawyers over the open video feed during court breaks, sometimes with the prosecution present.121 Throughout the trial, the sole allowance made for private consultations occurred at the hearing on June 19: when the court recessed, other participants were removed from the video feed to permit Ilyashev to consult with his defense team.122
explanation: 报告记录庭间通常无法保密沟通，6月19日曾允许一次私人咨询；该部分改善不等于整个沟通问题解决。

exactQuote: First, the Kazakh Supreme Court should use its power of judicial review and remedy the violations of Ilyashev’s right to a fair trial and right to freedom of expression detailed above. Specifically, the Court should overturn the appellate decision upholding Ilyashev’s conviction.
explanation: 专家呼吁最高法院纠正权利违反并推翻维持原判的上诉裁定；未把建议当已撤销定罪。

exactQuote: Third, video conferencing guidelines recently issued by the European Criminal Bar Association are instructive:226 among other things, the use of videoconferencing should require the consent of the accused; legal remedies should be readily available to challenge a decision on using videoconferencing; an accused’s right to speak confidentially with his or her defense team must be guaranteed at all times (before and during hearings); an uninterrupted and high-quality connection must be in place; accused persons must be provided a full view of the courtroom, and be able to observe all participants; and any technical arrangements should ensure that the virtual hearing resembles an in-person hearing to the greatest extent possible.
explanation: 作者提出远程审判的保密沟通和连线等保障建议；不表示这些保障在本案全部落实。

exactQuote: From July to November 2020, the Clooney Foundation for Justice’s TrialWatch initiative monitored the criminal trial of Alexander Pichugin in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia. Mr. Pichugin is a journalist and was also the anonymous administrator of a channel called “Sorokin Hvost” on online messaging platform Telegram . Mr. Pichugin was charged with violating Article 207.1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation, which makes it a crime to “publicly disseminate disguised as truthful knowingly false information about circumstances that pose a threat to the life and safety of citizens.”
explanation: 记录记者身份、Telegram 频道管理与指控；法条引述为历史背景。

exactQuote: The charges related to a sarcastic comment Mr. Pichugin made on “Sorkin Hvost” on April 12, 2020, which is celebrated by the Russian Orthodox Church as Palm Sunday, criticizing the holding of Easter services during the COVID-19 pandemic. In particular, Mr. Pichugin said that there was “ a planned campaign to infect the population with a deadly disease ” and likened participants in church services to “ adherers-suicide assassins” who would be used “as disseminators of infection ” and suggested the Church had gathered “them in specially designated places, where the distributors deliberately violate sanitary rules and then penetrate the society.”
explanation: 报告明确涉案发言是对疫情期间宗教活动的讽刺评论；不把指控当真实危险。

exactQuote: By contrast, the defense argued that the post was an opinion, not a statement of fact. A linguistic expert for the defense testified that the post was written in the form of a metaphor.36 Mr. Pichugin self -described the genre of the text as “sarcastic journalism” 37 and explained that to give people the opportunity to “look at the situation from the other side” he used “the method of detachment, alienation.” 38
explanation: 辩方主张意见而非事实，并由语言学专家说明比喻性质；属于庭审论点和证词。

exactQuote: Further, the defense pointed out that the prosecution’s expert’s opinion was flawed. In particular, during cross-examination, the expert admitted that the post had been presented to them for analysis as having come from a news channel, not as an anonymous post on a Telegram channel.40 On this basis, the defense petitioned the court for a supplementary linguistic examination. This petition was granted, and a court appointed linguistic expert report was prepared by the Federally-funded Institution “Privolzhsky Regional Forensic Center.” These additional experts concluded that Mr. Pichugin’s message included both facts (information that could be verified) and opinions (information that could not be verified). The experts also concluded that the message was constructed in the form of a metaphor and that the overall communicative goal was to share a personal opinion about the negative attitude the author had to the actions described in the message.41
explanation: 交叉询问后辩方请求补充语言学鉴定并获准；补充专家同时认定有事实与意见内容，不应简化为完全支持一方。

exactQuote: On November 11, 2020, the Bogorodsk City Court found Mr. Pichugin guilty and sentenced him to a fine of 300,000 rubles.
explanation: 报告记录定罪与罚金；之后的作者批评不改变这是已发生判决的记载。

exactQuote: The constitutional approach to the facts of the case would have been, on the one hand, to question the constitutionality of the law, which criminalises the alleged act of the accused, and on the other hand to identify the intention of the author independently.
explanation: 专家提出本应质疑法律合宪性并独立认定发言意图的评价；不是已经获得的救济。

exactQuote: Dian Abdullah is the author of the independent Malaysia FlipFlop Blog. On March 21 and 23, 2020, Abdullah published two posts in English criticizing, among other things, Prime Minister Muhyiddin and what she described as the inadequate support provided to those who lost employment as a result of the COVID-19 pandemic.[54]
explanation: 正文说明独立博客作者身份、两篇发言日期与批评主题；不自动归类职业记者。

exactQuote: In June 2020, Abdullah was charged in two instruments with, respectively, “ma[king] statements . . . with intent to cause, or that may cause fear or unrest to the public or to any sections of the public”[2] under Section 505(b) of the Malaysian Penal Code and “consciously ma[king] and commenc[ing] the communication delivery that is abhorrent in nature . . . with intent to oﬀend other people’s feelings”[3] under Section 233(1)(a) of the Communications and Multimedia Act (CMA). The Section 505(b) charge stemmed from a blog post made on March 21, 2020 and the Section 233(1) charge stemmed from a blog post made on March 23, 2020. explanation: 摘要明确2020年6月的两组指控及所引法条；这不是定罪。

exactQuote: Going forward, prosecutors and judges should carefully review proposed charges under Section 505 and Section 233 to ensure that that the criminal conduct at issue is suﬃciently grave to warrant a criminal prosecution and that there is a demonstrated and articulated link between the speech and the threat, in line with international standards on freedom of expression.
